summary: Go covers the core notebook cell mutation path, and several earlier gaps have already been partly addressed, but it is still not TS-exact. The highest-risk divergences are model-visible output/error payloads, target validation, stale-read and permission gates, notebook JSON serialization fidelity, file-history lifecycle behavior, and parity tests that still encode stale or Go-only assumptions.

gaps.title: Success and error payloads do not match the TS outputSchema or tool_result mapping
ts_evidence: ../src/tools/NotebookEditTool/NotebookEditTool.ts:60-84 defines the output schema as new_source, cell_id, cell_type, language, edit_mode, error, notebook_path, original_file, and updated_file.
../src/tools/NotebookEditTool/NotebookEditTool.ts:133-171 maps a populated error field to an is_error tool_result and maps successful edit modes to mode-specific text.
../src/tools/NotebookEditTool/NotebookEditTool.ts:335-347,443-455,457-487 return the same structured data shape for parse errors, successes, and caught errors.
go_evidence: tools/notebook.go:37-46 defines NotebookEditResult as file_path, cell_id, edit_mode, cell_index, before, after, edit_id, and execution_count_reset.
tools/notebook.go:54-78 marshals both snake_case and camelCase aliases, which are not the TS NotebookEdit output fields.
tools/notebook.go:145-229 returns plain error strings with IsError=true for validation, read, parse, and apply errors.
tools/notebook.go:277-291 returns JSON for the Go-specific NotebookEditResult without new_source, cell_type, language, notebook_path, original_file, updated_file, or error.

gaps.title: Cell target validation is looser than TS and permits hidden addressing modes
ts_evidence: ../src/tools/NotebookEditTool/NotebookEditTool.ts:260-267 rejects missing cell_id for non-insert modes.
../src/tools/NotebookEditTool/NotebookEditTool.ts:269-290 resolves only an actual cell id or a cell-N fallback and rejects missing or out-of-range targets.
../src/utils/notebook.ts:217-224 parseCellId accepts only the /^cell-(\d+)$/ form.
go_evidence: tools/notebook.go:144-174 validates path, cell_type, edit_mode, and insert cell_type, but does not reject missing cell_id for replace.
tools/notebook_apply_edit.go:54-70 lets replace with an empty cell_id edit the first cell when the notebook is non-empty.
tools/notebook_cell_id.go:9-64 supports Go-only targeting forms including last, bare positive integers, and negative indexes.
tools/notebook_apply_edit.go:130-145 also accepts bare integer positional references during replace-to-insert promotion.

gaps.title: Read-before-edit exists, but stale-read detection is missing
ts_evidence: ../src/tools/NotebookEditTool/NotebookEditTool.ts:218-237 requires a prior read and rejects the edit if the notebook mtime is newer than the recorded read timestamp.
../src/tools/NotebookEditTool/NotebookEditTool.ts:433-442 refreshes readFileState after a successful write so later reads and edits see the updated content.
go_evidence: tools/notebook.go:176-193 checks only whether a ReadState entry exists.
tools/notebook.go:195-220 reads and parses the current file immediately after the existence check without comparing os.Stat mtime to ReadFileEntry.TimestampMs.
tools/file_read_state.go:21-47 already stores TimestampMs, IsPartialView, Content, and LastTool, so the data needed for a stale-read guard is available.
tools/notebook.go:259-275 refreshes read state after write, but the pre-write stale check is absent.

gaps.title: NotebookEdit is not wired to the same write permission/path-scope checks as TS
ts_evidence: ../src/tools/NotebookEditTool/NotebookEditTool.ts:122-131 exposes getPath and delegates checkPermissions to checkWritePermissionForTool.

../src/components/permissions/NotebookEditPermissionRequest/NotebookEditPermissionRequest.tsx:32-136 renders the NotebookEdit write confirmation dialog with path, operation, language, and diff content.
../src/tools/NotebookEditTool/NotebookEditTool.ts:180-187 has a UNC-path guard before filesystem validation to avoid credential leaks.
go_evidence: tools/notebook.go:84-89 defines NotebookEditTool with only ReadState and no AllowedDirs, permission, or plan/write-scope fields.
registry_setup.go:328-329 registers NotebookEditTool with only ReadState injected.
tools/notebook.go:195 and tools/notebook.go:255 read and write in.NotebookPath directly; no checkAllowedPath call appears in the NotebookEdit path.
tools/file_operations.go:15-45 provides checkAllowedPath for other tools, but NotebookEdit does not use it.

gaps.title: Notebook JSON round-trip is not fidelity-preserving
ts_evidence: ../src/tools/NotebookEditTool/NotebookEditTool.ts:331-333 parses the whole notebook object and mutates it in place.
../src/tools/NotebookEditTool/NotebookEditTool.ts:397-412 creates inserted cells with source set to the new_source string.
../src/tools/NotebookEditTool/NotebookEditTool.ts:417-427 replaces only targetCell.source and optional targetCell.cell_type, leaving other cell fields on the parsed object intact.
../src/tools/NotebookEditTool/NotebookEditTool.ts:430-432 serializes the mutated notebook object back with jsonStringify.
go_evidence: tools/notebook_parse.go:21-37 models only nbformat, nbformat_minor, metadata, cells, and a limited Cell shape.
tools/notebook_parse.go:49-56 models only id, cell_type, source, metadata, outputs, and execution_count for cells.
tools/notebook_parse.go:97-103 assigns ids to existing id-less cells during parse for nbformat 4.5+, which TS NotebookEdit does not do during edit.
tools/notebook_parse.go:114-124 serializes only the modeled fields, dropping unknown top-level or per-cell fields.
tools/notebook_apply_edit.go:81,162,193 stores new source as split []string, while TS writes the new_source string.

gaps.title: Code-cell execution_count and outputs are omitted instead of written as TS writes them
ts_evidence: ../src/tools/NotebookEditTool/NotebookEditTool.ts:405-412 inserts code cells with execution_count: null and outputs: [].
../src/tools/NotebookEditTool/NotebookEditTool.ts:420-424 resets edited code cells with execution_count = null and outputs = [].
go_evidence: tools/notebook_parse.go:35-36 tags outputs and execution_count with omitempty.
tools/notebook_outputs.go:32-35 ClearOutputs returns nil.
tools/notebook_apply_edit.go:88-89 sets Outputs to nil and ExecutionCount to nil on replace, which serializes as omission due to omitempty.
tools/notebook_apply_edit.go:159-165 and tools/notebook_apply_edit.go:190-196 build inserted cells without a serializable null execution_count and with empty outputs that are omitted.

gaps.title: File encoding, line endings, and mode handling differ from TS writeTextContent flow
ts_evidence: ../src/utils/fileRead.ts:75-98 readFileSyncWithMetadata returns normalized content plus original encoding and line ending style.
../src/utils/file.ts:84-98 writeTextContent writes using the detected encoding and restores CRLF when the original file used CRLF.
../src/tools/NotebookEditTool/NotebookEditTool.ts:320-325 and ../src/tools/NotebookEditTool/NotebookEditTool.ts:430-432 thread encoding and lineEndings through the NotebookEdit write.
go_evidence: tools/notebook.go:195 reads raw bytes with os.ReadFile and does not capture encoding or line ending metadata.
tools/notebook_parse.go:131-135 uses json.MarshalIndent and appends a LF newline unconditionally.
tools/notebook.go:255 writes with atomicWriteFile using a fixed 0644 permission instead of preserving target file mode or TS writeTextContent semantics.
tools/atomic.go:44-46 applies the passed permission to the temp file before rename.

gaps.title: TS file-history lifecycle is missing, while Go adds a TS-unproven metadata side effect
ts_evidence: ../src/tools/NotebookEditTool/NotebookEditTool.ts:311-317 calls fileHistoryTrackEdit before modifying the notebook when file history is enabled.
../src/tools/NotebookEditTool/NotebookEditTool.ts:443-453 exposes original_file and updated_file in the tool output for attribution/recovery consumers.
../src/tools/NotebookEditTool/NotebookEditTool.ts:397-427 does not add a metadata.claude stamp while mutating cells.
go_evidence: registry_setup.go:188-204 constructs HistoryStore for FileWriteTool and FileEditTool, but registry_setup.go:328-329 registers NotebookEditTool without a history store.
tools/notebook.go:243-249 stamps edited cells with SetEditedBy and rewrites the after snapshot.
tools/notebook_attribution.go:7-24 writes metadata.claude = {editedBy, editedAt, sessionId?}, a notebook mutation not present in the TS NotebookEdit path.
tools/notebook.go:277-291 does not return original_file or updated_file, so Go lacks the TS recovery payload even though it adds edit_id/before/after.

gaps.title: NotebookEdit input is not strict-object equivalent
ts_evidence: ../src/tools/NotebookEditTool/NotebookEditTool.ts:30-56 uses z.strictObject, so unknown input properties are rejected by the TS schema.
../src/tools/NotebookEditTool/NotebookEditTool.ts:44-52 uses enums for cell_type and edit_mode.
go_evidence: types/tools.go:9-15 defines JSONSchema without an AdditionalProperties field, so the emitted schema cannot express strictObject.
tools/helpers.go:22-38 parses tool input by json.Marshal followed by json.Unmarshal into a struct; Go's default unmarshal ignores unknown fields.
tools/notebook.go:107-135 emits properties and required fields for NotebookEdit, but does not express additionalProperties=false.

gaps.title: Go has an extra large-notebook refusal path not evidenced in the TS NotebookEdit implementation
ts_evidence: ../src/tools/NotebookEditTool/NotebookEditTool.ts:90-99 sets maxResultSizeChars and prompt metadata, but the call path does not define a notebook input-size refusal.
../src/tools/NotebookEditTool/NotebookEditTool.ts:319-333 reads and parses the notebook content directly before mutation.
go_evidence: tools/notebook.go:17-21 defines MaxNotebookEditSize as 32 MiB.
tools/notebook.go:200-215 rejects notebooks larger than MaxNotebookEditSize with a jq hint before parsing or editing.
tools/notebook_wave2_test.go:207-245 locks in the Go-specific large-notebook jq-hint behavior.

gaps.title: NotebookEdit tests contain stale or Go-only parity assumptions
ts_evidence: ../src/tools/NotebookEditTool/NotebookEditTool.ts:60-84 has no edit_id, before, after, file_path, cell_index, or execution_count_reset fields in the TS outputSchema.
../src/tools/NotebookEditTool/NotebookEditTool.ts:218-237 requires a prior read before edit.
go_evidence: tools/notebook_alignment_test.go:169-196 asserts before/after snapshots as if they were TS parity fields.
tools/notebook_alignment_test.go:269-325 asserts execution_count_reset and edit_id fields that are Go-only relative to the TS outputSchema.

tools/notebook_conformance_test.go:287-310,337-360,362-376,394-427 instantiate a bare NotebookEditTool and expect successful edits without seeding ReadState, conflicting with tools/notebook.go:176-193.
tools/notebook_conformance_test.go:147-163 still names TestApplyEditReplacePreservesOutputs even though tools/notebook_apply_edit.go:84-89 now clears outputs on every code source replace.

candidate_tasks.title: Restore the TS NotebookEdit output and error contract
acceptance: Successful NotebookEdit responses expose the TS fields new_source, cell_id, cell_type, language, edit_mode, error, notebook_path, original_file, and updated_file.

Go-only top-level fields such as file_path, before, after, edit_id, cell_index, execution_count_reset, and camelCase aliases are removed from the model-visible TS parity result or moved behind a clearly non-TS internal surface.
Tool-level errors return a payload consistent with TS data.error behavior and map to IsError/tool_result error semantics.
Result tests cover replace, insert, delete, invalid JSON, missing cell, and write failure shapes.

candidate_tasks.title: Tighten cell target validation to TS validateInput semantics
acceptance: Replace and delete without cell_id are rejected before mutation.
Target lookup accepts only exact ids and cell-N positional fallback, matching TS parseCellId; last, bare integers, and negative indexes are not accepted through NotebookEdit.
Out-of-range cell-N targets are rejected at validation time.
Insert without cell_id still inserts at the beginning, and insert with cell_id inserts after the resolved target.

candidate_tasks.title: Add NotebookEdit stale-read detection
acceptance: NotebookEdit rejects when os.Stat mtime is newer than ReadFileEntry.TimestampMs, using the same message intent as TS.
Successful NotebookEdit refreshes ReadState with post-write content and mtime so immediate subsequent edits do not require a new read.
Tests cover unread, stale-read, and post-write read-state refresh cases.

candidate_tasks.title: Wire NotebookEdit to write permission/path scope and absolute path handling
acceptance: NotebookEditTool has an AllowedDirs or equivalent write-scope dependency and registry_setup.go injects the session allowedDirs.
NotebookEdit validates the resolved notebook path with the same path-scope helper used by write/edit tools before reading or writing.
Read/write operations use the resolved absolute path consistently for filesystem access and ReadState keys.
Permission/path tests cover outside-allowed-dir rejection, symlink escape behavior consistent with the local file tools, and relative path normalization.

candidate_tasks.title: Preserve notebook JSON fields, source representation, and existing cell ids
acceptance: Unknown top-level notebook fields and unknown per-cell fields survive parse-edit-serialize round trips.
Editing an existing id-less cell does not synthesize a persistent id unless TS would write one for a new inserted cell.
New or replaced source fields are serialized in the TS shape for NotebookEdit, not forcibly split into []string.
Tests include fixtures with attachments, unknown metadata, custom top-level keys, id-less cells, string source, and array source.

candidate_tasks.title: Match TS code-cell execution_count, outputs, encoding, and line-ending behavior
dependencies: NE-T05 is helpful if raw JSON preservation is implemented first, but this can be developed with targeted serializers.
acceptance: Inserted code cells serialize execution_count:null and outputs:[] like TS.
Edited code cells serialize execution_count:null and outputs:[] after source replacement.
Markdown cells do not gain code-only execution/output fields.
NotebookEdit preserves original CRLF-vs-LF behavior and detected encoding in the same spirit as TS readFileSyncWithMetadata/writeTextContent.
NotebookEdit does not force an existing file mode to 0644 when replacing the notebook.

candidate_tasks.title: Align file-history lifecycle and remove or gate Go-only attribution mutation
dependencies: NE-T01 should define whether original_file/updated_file carry the recovery payload.
acceptance: NotebookEdit has the same file-history tracking lifecycle as TS when history is enabled.
registry_setup.go injects any required shared history store into NotebookEdit.
metadata.claude attribution is removed from the default TS-parity write path or explicitly gated outside the TS-parity behavior.
Tests prove file-history entries are created for NotebookEdit and existing notebook metadata is not modified by Go-only attribution in parity mode.

candidate_tasks.title: Enforce strict NotebookEdit input object behavior
acceptance: NotebookEdit rejects unknown input keys in the same way TS z.strictObject does.

The emitted schema or local validation documents/expresses additionalProperties=false for NotebookEdit if the shared JSONSchema type supports it; otherwise NotebookEdit performs an explicit key whitelist check.
Tests cover unknown keys, invalid enum values, missing required values, and valid minimal replace/insert/delete inputs.

candidate_tasks.title: Resolve the extra large-notebook guard against the TS baseline
acceptance: Either remove the Go-only MaxNotebookEditSize refusal from the TS-parity path, or document and gate it as an intentional non-parity safety extension.
If retained, tests assert the feature gate/extension mode; if removed, tests assert large notebooks flow to the same parse/write behavior and result-size handling as the TS tool.
The reportable behavior is consistent with maxResultSize/tool result handling decided in NE-T01.

candidate_tasks.title: Refresh NotebookEdit parity tests so they prove TS behavior instead of stale Go assumptions
dependencies: Can start immediately by marking TS-contract expectations; final green state depends on NE-T01 through NE-T09 implementation choices.
acceptance: Tests no longer describe resolved historical gaps as current failures.
Tests stop treating Go-only fields such as edit_id, before, after, file_path, and execution_count_reset as TS parity requirements.
Tool-level success tests seed ReadState correctly, while unread/stale tests intentionally exercise the guard.
Every high-risk gap above has at least one focused failing/passing test with TS evidence in the test comment or fixture name.
